reasoning_summary: The run used simpleFoam with steadyState time scheme. At the configured Reynolds number of 100.0 the wake is expected to shed vortices, and a steady solver cannot capture this unsteady behaviour.
The Strouhal number was not obtained (strouhal_number is null). The rms lift coefficient is 0.0, so no oscillation was resolved. One requested quantity is therefore missing entirely.

The reported mean drag coefficient of 1.0921 is the steady-solver value. It is not a time-mean over shedding cycles. The evidence has no stationary window, no averaging, and no stationary cycles (all null), so it cannot be trusted to 3 %.

The mesh is coarse for this problem. The representative cell size is 0.45745 D, the wake last cell is 1.0209 D, and the first wall cell is 0.005 D. The wake is under-resolved, and the first-order-like upwinding-dominated steady solution is further smeared.

The outlet pressure is fixedValue and the inlet pressure is zeroGradient, which is standard. The inlet is uniform and the blockage is 0.0125, so the setup is not the main problem. The steady-versus-unsteady mismatch and the missing Strouhal number are enough to reject.
